newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks clarify latest Holocaust fund pledge.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks clarify latest Holocaust fund pledge.

text.p: Swiss banks said on Wednesday that 20 million Swiss francs ($13.7 million) pledged this week for a Holocaust memorial fund was money already promised by a broader Swiss industry group, not an additional payment.

The Swiss Bankers' Association, which said on Tuesday that its smaller members would put up the 20 milllion francs, told reporters the figure was actually a confirmation of an amount that had already been included in a pledge of 65 million from the Swiss commerce and industry assocation Vorort.
"The Vorort announcement of 65 million was based on an estimate of what the banks would donate. We only received the confirmation from our members last week," a bankers' association spokeswoman said.
This means the total pledged so far to the memorial fund for Holocaust survivors remains 265 million Swiss francs, not 285 million as reported on Tuesday.

The fund was launched last month with a 100-million-franc donation from the three biggest banks. Other companies and smaller banks joined in a collective pledge of 65 million and the Swiss National Bank plans to chip in 100 million.
Confusion over the latest pledge stemmed from a statement by the Swiss Bankers' Association on Tuesday on its smaller members' reaction to the initial step by the three biggest banks.

"On the basis of firm pledges, the Swiss Bankers' Association can state that more than 20 million francs in additional funds will shortly be paid into the special fund as a contribution from other banks," the banking industry group said.
International pressure and threats of boycotts galvanised big Swiss banks to start the fund, which is being coordinated by the Swiss government in Berne and world Jewish groups.

The memorial fund is separate from the seven-billion-franc Swiss Solidarity Foundation proposed by Berne that would sell official gold reserves to finance aid for victims of poverty, catastrophes and human rights abuses, including the Holocaust. ($ = 1.462 Swiss Francs)
